title: Feldspar flotation as a quartz-purification method in cosmogenic nuclide dating: A case study of fluvial sediments from the Pamir
author: Sulaymonova, Fuchs, et al.

steps.title: Crush and sieve samples
steps.instruction: Crush the sediment and wet‑sieve into 250–500 µm and 500–1000 µm grain‑size fractions.

steps.title: Dry and subsample for XRD
steps.instruction: Dry the sieved fractions and take representative subsamples for X‑ray diffraction (XRD) analysis.

steps.title: Remove strongly magnetic minerals
steps.instruction: Use a hand magnet to pull out strongly magnetic minerals, then run the residue through a Frantz magnetic separator to isolate mica and chlorite.

steps.title: XRD after magnetic separation
steps.instruction: Take subsamples of the magnetically separated material for XRD analysis.

steps.title: Acid digestion of carbonates and organics
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1:1 (v/v) solution of HCl (32 %) and H₂SiF₆ (34 %). Add this solution to the sample to dissolve carbonates, feldspar, and organic material.

steps.title: Shake overnight
steps.instruction: Place the acid‑treated sample in 250 mL polyethylene bottles, shake horizontally at room temperature, and leave overnight.

steps.title: Decant and rinse
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant and rinse the solid repeatedly with deionized water until the rinse water is clear.

steps.title: Repeat acid wash cycles
steps.instruction: Perform six consecutive acid‑wash cycles using the same 1:1 HCl/H₂SiF₆ solution, each followed by decanting and rinsing as described.

steps.title: Assemble flotation cell
steps.instruction: Fit the three glass parts together: lower part 8.5 cm high × 10 cm diameter with two 0.6 cm holes for air tubes; middle part 16 cm high × 9.5 cm diameter containing an 8 cm diameter ceramic frit (thickness 0.6 cm, porosity 2, pore size 40–100 µm); upper part 24 cm long × 2.5 cm diameter that bends to form a tube inclined 15° from horizontal with a 1 cm‑diameter flexible collection tube attached. Place the assembled cell on a magnetic plate to allow stirring.

steps.title: Prepare dodecylamine collector
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g dodecylamine (98 %) in 5.4 mL 1 N HCl and 100 mL deionized water; keep 6 mL of this collector solution ready for use.

steps.title: Start air pump
steps.instruction: Turn on a compressed‑air aquarium pump (≈0.00443 Pa pressure) so air flows through the lower‑part holes, rises through the ceramic frit, and generates bubbles.

steps.title: Load HF‑wetted sample
steps.instruction: Add up to 90 g of the pre‑treated sample to the middle part of the cell; the sample must already be wetted with 0.2 % HF.

steps.title: Add collector and adjust pH
steps.instruction: Add 6 mL of the dodecylamine collector solution to the HF‑sample mixture, then cover the mixture with additional 0.2 % HF so the liquid level is above the flexible‑tube opening; adjust the pH to 2.4–2.7 using 1 N H₂SO₄ or deionized water.

steps.title: Stir and float
steps.instruction: Activate the magnetic stirrer at 5 rpm to mix the slurry while the air pump continues; conduct flotation at room temperature for ≤2 h (shorter if feldspar content is low).

steps.title: Collect feldspar fraction
steps.instruction: Allow bubbles to rise, burst at the liquid‑air interface, and release feldspar grains into the attached flexible tube; retrieve the collected feldspar.

steps.title: Recover quartz
steps.instruction: Filter the remaining quartz from the slurry, rinse the filter cake with 5 % HCl, wash with deionized water, and dry the quartz at temperatures below 60 °C.

steps.title: Optional feldspar treatment
steps.instruction: Treat the recovered feldspar fraction in the same way (5 % HCl rinse, water wash, dry <60 °C) if it will be used for other nuclide analyses.
